title: Bulk Criticality and Boundary Spectra in AdS from Matrix Product States
abstract: We study interacting scalar quantum field theories in anti-de Sitter (AdS) space using a tensor-network approach based on matrix product states. We develop methods for extracting low-lying boundary spectra from global-AdS energy levels, probing bulk criticality through finite-size scaling in the AdS radius, and identifying conformal boundary conditions. Applying these methods to scalar $φ^4$ theory in $\mathrm{AdS}_2$, we compute the lowest non-trivial $\mathbb{Z}_2$-odd and even boundary scaling dimensions non-perturbatively. We then locate the bulk $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry-breaking transition and extract critical exponents and central charge consistent with the 2D Ising universality class. At the critical point, we determine the low-lying boundary spectrum and use it to identify the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-preserving free/ordinary Ising conformal boundary condition, thereby characterising both the bulk and boundary universality classes.
summary: This paper applies tensor-network methods, specifically Matrix Product States, to study interacting quantum field theories in Anti-de Sitter space. By analyzing the energy spectrum and performing finite-size scaling, the authors non-perturbatively characterize the critical point of $\phi^4$ theory in $	ext{AdS}_2$. This work successfully maps the bulk and boundary physics onto the known 2D Ising universality class.
main_problem: The study investigates interacting quantum field theories in Anti-de Sitter (AdS) space, focusing on determining bulk criticality and extracting the low-lying boundary spectra.
main_result: The authors successfully compute boundary scaling dimensions non-perturbatively for $\phi^4$ theory in $	ext{AdS}_2$, locating the bulk $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry-breaking transition consistent with the 2D Ising universality class.
method: The research employs a tensor-network approach based on Matrix Product States (MPS) and utilizes finite-size scaling in the AdS radius ($R$) to probe critical behavior.
model_or_system: The system is an interacting scalar quantum field theory, specifically $\phi^4$ theory, formulated in global Anti-de Sitter space ($	ext{AdS}_2$). The Hamiltonian is discretized using a lattice formulation.
key_observables: Low-lying boundary spectra, bulk energy levels, critical exponents, and central charge.
important_parameters: The AdS radius ($R$), the coupling constant ($\lambda$), and the lattice spacing.
main_assumptions: The use of a lattice Hamiltonian formulation allows for independent variation of the lattice spacing and the AdS radius $R$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework by relating the global AdS spectrum to boundary operators via the bulk-boundary OPE. It then details the lattice discretization of the Hamiltonian and applies the MPS/tensor-network methods to compute spectra and analyze finite-size scaling near critical points.
why_interesting: The application of tensor networks (MPS) to study critical phenomena in curved spacetime provides a powerful, non-perturbative tool for analyzing strongly correlated quantum systems, bridging condensed matter critical theory with gravity/QFT.
